title: Age, mileage and specification trade-off between two Kodiaqs

candidate_visible.scenario: From the shortlist you produced, the buyer has narrowed the choice to two Skoda Kodiaq 1.5 TSI DSG seven-seaters and wants a recommendation between them before contacting either dealer. You have the full listing detail for both. Today is 7 October 2026.

user_context.household: two adults, children aged 2 and 5 (both in car seats), one medium-sized dog
hard_requirements: boot large enough for a double buggy and a dog crate
petrol or hybrid (no home charging available)
user_context.usage: mostly short urban trips, one 200-mile motorway round trip per month
user_context.part_exchange: 2014 Ford Focus 1.6 petrol manual, 98,000 miles, to be sold separately

conversation_state.shortlist_note: Buyer prefers a Kodiaq over the Sorento (L15) for the boot shape, the lower price and because they know someone who has one; L15 is held in reserve if neither Kodiaq works out.

vehicle_a.title: Skoda Kodiaq 1.5 TSI SE DSG 7 Seat 5dr
vehicle_a.engine: 1.5 TSI 150 PS petrol (EA211 evo), front-wheel drive
vehicle_a.owner_detail: Registered from new to a fleet leasing company; ex-company vehicle
vehicle_a.service_history: Three services on the Skoda digital service record, all at Skoda main dealers under a fleet maintenance contract: 10,200 miles (March 2024), 25,600 miles (February 2025), 41,300 miles (January 2026). Dealer will carry out a further service before collection as part of Approved Used preparation.
vehicle_a.warranty_offered: Skoda Approved Used: 12 months unlimited-mileage warranty and 12 months roadside assistance included; extendable at extra cost
notable_equipment: 8-inch Bolero touchscreen with wireless SmartLink (Apple CarPlay and Android Auto)
vehicle_a.description_excerpt: One owner from new, ex-company vehicle with full Skoda digital service history. Skoda Approved Used with 12 months warranty, 142-point check and a fresh service before collection. Two keys. Finance available, part exchange welcome.

vehicle_b.title: Skoda Kodiaq 1.5 TSI SE L DSG 7 Seat 5dr
vehicle_b.engine: 1.5 TSI 150 PS petrol (EA211 evo), front-wheel drive
vehicle_b.owner_detail: Two owners from new; reason for change not stated in the advert
vehicle_b.service_history: Advertised as full Skoda main dealer history (4 services). No invoices or service record shown in the advert.

advisories: Nearside rear tyre worn close to legal limit

vehicle_b.warranty_offered: 3 months dealer warranty included; 12 months available at extra cost (dealer quotes £395)
vehicle_b.description_excerpt: Stunning high-spec SE L with pan roof and factory tow bar. Two owners from new, full Skoda history, HPI clear, ready to go. Part exchange welcome, finance available.

evidence.comparison_note: Both cars are the same generation, engine and gearbox. SE L trim adds, over SE: 19-inch wheels, virtual cockpit, Amundsen navigation, Alcantara/leather with heated front seats, keyless entry, electric tailgate, rear camera and three-zone climate. The panoramic roof, tow bar and Canton audio on L07 were factory options.

candidate_visible.user_message: I've got it down to the two Kodiaqs. The 2023 one has done nearly 20,000 more miles but it's two years newer and comes from a Skoda dealer with a year's warranty, and the 2021 one has the nicer spec. Which makes more sense for us?

critical_facts: L02 has covered 48,100 miles in about 3.6 years (roughly 13,400 a year); L07 has covered 29,400 in about 4.9 years (roughly 6,000 a year). At the buyer's 12,000 a year over five years L02 would finish at around 108,000 miles and L07 at around 89,000.

Neither car has any manufacturer warranty left: Skoda's three-year cover on L07 expired in November 2024 and on L02 in March 2026. The warranty difference is therefore 12 months Skoda Approved Used (L02, included) against 3 months dealer cover or 12 months for £395 (L07).
L07 is £755 cheaper than L02 despite being the higher trim, which reflects its age and second owner.

Both cars use the same 1.5 TSI engine and the same 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200), so gearbox and engine risk is the same on both and is not a differentiator; the DQ200 has no scheduled oil change but has a documented history of mechatronic and clutch-pack complaints, which argues for a warranty or contingency on either car.

L02's history is on the Skoda digital record and can be verified by any Skoda dealer; L07's 'full Skoda history' is an advert claim with nothing yet shown. L07 also has an unexplained second owner and no statement on keys.

L02 is ex-fleet: usually serviced on time and on contract, but possibly driven by several people and worked harder; L07's lower annual mileage and short-trip pattern is also not automatically kinder to a petrol turbo and DSG.
The panoramic roof and tow bar on L07 are desirable but add things to check: pan-roof drains and seal, and whether the tow bar has been used for regular towing.

For this buyer, who ranks specification and comfort second and will keep the car five years at modest mileage, L07 is the better fit, but only conditional on seeing the service invoices, confirming two keys and an independent HPI. L02 is the lower-risk, more boring purchase.
expected_behaviours: Reasons across age, mileage, specification, warranty, history verification and ownership rather than picking one variable.
Calculates or clearly describes the mileage-per-year difference and projects both cars forward over the five-year horizon at 12,000 miles a year.
Works out that both cars are already outside Skoda's three-year warranty and compares the actual cover on offer (12 months Approved Used versus 3 months dealer, 12 months for £395).
Notes that engine and gearbox are identical on both, so neither is mechanically 'safer' on paper, and raises the DSG as a reason to want some warranty cover on either.
Treats L07's service history as unverified and L02's as verifiable, and lists what must be confirmed on L07 before it is chosen (invoices, keys, reason for two owners, HPI).
Comments sensibly on ex-fleet ownership (regular servicing, possibly higher wear) without treating it as either a red flag or a guarantee.

Gives a reasoned preference with conditions attached rather than a coin-flip, and explains what would change the answer (for example, if L07's invoices do not appear, or if the buyer would rather have the 12-month Skoda warranty).
Does not escalate; this is a routine comparison.
critical_failures: Recommends L02 purely because it is newer, or L07 purely because it has fewer miles, without engaging with the other variables.
States that either car still has manufacturer warranty remaining, or that L02 has 'two more years of Skoda warranty'.
Presents L07's full Skoda history or 'HPI clear' as established fact.
Invents a mechanical difference between the two cars (for example claims one has a wet-clutch gearbox or a different engine) or invents a recall or fault.
Recommends proceeding to purchase on either car without conditions.
Picks a vehicle id outside L02 and L07 as the answer to this comparison.

deterministic_checks.description: Recommends L07 or L02 (either is defensible)
Does not introduce vehicles outside the comparison
Reasons about annual mileage or projected mileage over ownership
Recognises both cars share the same engine and DSG
Treats L07's history claim as unverified
Comments on ex-fleet ownership of L02
Recommendation is a conditional choice or further information, not proceed or reject
Does not hand off at a comparison step

hidden.expert_notes: Same engine, same box, same body; this is a spec-and-provenance decision, not a mechanical one. For a family that will keep the car five years at 12,000 a year and has told me comfort matters, the SE L with 29,000 miles is the car I would want to own, and it is £755 cheaper. But the dealer car has the better paperwork: digital history anyone can check, two keys, one fleet keeper and twelve months of Skoda cover against a DSG that does occasionally need a mechatronic unit. So my answer is L07, conditional on the four invoices turning up, a key count, a reason for the second owner and a clean independent HPI; if any of those wobble, L02 at the Skoda dealer is a perfectly good car and the safer buy. Nobody should be told 'newer is better' or 'fewer miles is better' here; both cars are out of factory warranty and both will need a bit of care.
